takeaway: The inguinal canal roof is internal oblique and transversalis; floor is the inguinal and lacunar ligaments; back wall is transversalis fascia and conjoint tendon.

question.text: Which one of the following statements regarding the inguinal canal is correct?

answer.text: The roof consists of the internal oblique and transversalis muscles.

lines.text: The inguinal canal is about 4 cm long, running from the deep ring to the superficial ring.
lines.say: The inguinal canal is about four centimetres long, running from the deep ring to the superficial ring.

lines.text: It carries the spermatic cord in men, and the round ligament in women.
Now picture the canal as a little house. The roof is the internal oblique and the transversalis muscle.
The floor is the inguinal and lacunar ligaments.
And the back wall is the transversalis fascia and the conjoint tendon.
Options A and B mix up the floor and the back wall, so they are wrong.
So the correct statement is the roof: internal oblique and transversalis.
